In 30 seconds

What it is
A FastAPI and React/D3 tutor for six tree structures. Rule-based validators check every invariant after an operation; Gemini writes explanations and Socratic prompts, with rule-based fallbacks when no API key is set.
Whose it is
A team project with Niraj Chavan; the repository is his. The rotation lab on this page is a local demonstration I built that follows the tutor’s balance-factor rules.
What came of it
I co-authored an accepted manuscript on concept-level learning and misconception repair. The implementation figures here describe the public repository.

01 — Tree tutorCase studyCh. 01 / 08

01 — Problem

Students learn balanced-tree rules by memorising rotations.

The tutor takes the other route: it checks a structure against its invariants, names the rule involved, and links the mistake to prerequisite concepts. A language model can explain a rule, but it should not be the thing that decides whether the tree is valid.

Correctness
Rule-based validators, not the model, decide whether a structure is valid.
Availability
Every LLM path has a rule-based fallback, so the tutor works without an API key.
Scope
Six structures: AVL, red-black, B-tree, B+ tree, heap and segment tree.
Learning signal
Mastery moves only on deliberate evidence: quizzes, remediation and diagram checks.

2×

Each invariant is checked twice: inside the tree class and again on the exported JSON, and the results are merged.

agents/validation_agent.py @ 87d8dd0

03 — Tree tutorCase studyCh. 03 / 08

03 — Technical architecture

Five agents run in sequence over a shared blackboard for each tree operation. Validation sits in the middle and is never skipped.

Fig. 2.3 · Tree tutor architecture, full

Scroll sideways to follow the whole drawing.
  1. 1Student. Inserts, deletes and searches; takes quizzes; chats with the tutor; uploads diagrams.
  2. 2React and D3 interface. Animates each step and draws the concept graph.
  3. 3FastAPI. 33 HTTP routes and one WebSocket route for tutor chat.
  4. 4Operation pipeline. Agents share one blackboard instead of calling each other.
  5. 5A1 Execute. Runs the operation and returns the tree and a step log.
  6. 6A2 Validate. Internal and external validators check the invariants; results are merged and deduplicated.
  7. 7A3 Diagnose. Runs only if there are violations; the misconception engine holds 24 violation signatures.
  8. 8A4 Teach. An explanation and a guiding question; Gemini writes them, else a fallback bank.
  9. 9A5 Concept graph. 52 concepts and 94 edges with decay; the playground gives recommendations but never changes mastery.
  10. 10A6 Quiz. A 55-question bank; a graded answer moves mastery up or down.
  11. 11Tutoring layer. Socratic replies, sentiment and diagram grading; builds a learning path from weak concepts.
  12. 12Gemini 2.5 Flash. Optional enrichment; every call has a rule-based fallback.
04 — Tree tutorCase studyCh. 04 / 08

04 — Key challenges and decisions

  1. D1

    Validators are the source of truth.

    The LLM only explains, and every LLM path has a deterministic fallback.

    Trade-offThe validators only see trees built by the tool’s own self-balancing code, so the symbolic path rarely fires in normal use.

  2. D2

    A blackboard, not agent-to-agent calls.

    A conditional pipeline over one shared context: diagnosis runs only when validation finds a violation.

  3. D3

    Validate twice, report once.

    Invariants are checked inside the tree class and again on the exported JSON; the two result sets are merged and deduplicated.

  4. D4

    Mastery moves only on evidence.

    Quizzes, remediation and diagram checks change mastery. It decays on a forgetting curve, and mistakes propagate down the prerequisite graph.

  5. D5

    Explain every step.

    Each animation step carries a “why” and a concept tag, so a rotation is never just movement on screen.

05 — Tree tutorCase studyCh. 05 / 08

05 — Implementation and technology

A Python backend that owns the rules, and a React and D3 front end that shows each step.

The tutor tracks likely misconceptions from quiz answers and tutor conversations. Gemini writes explanations, Socratic prompts and quiz feedback; without an API key, the same paths return rule-based text. A Docker Compose setup runs the stack.

Backend
Python, FastAPI (34 routes), NetworkX
Language model
Gemini 2.5 Flash via google-generativeai, with rule-based fallbacks
Interface
React 18, Vite, D3 v7, Zustand, WebSocket
Delivery
Docker Compose; Celery and Redis optional; a PostgreSQL schema that is not wired in

04 — How it works

A local demonstration I built that follows the tutor’s balance-factor rules. Pick a node, rotate it, and the validator re-checks every node after each move.

Lab 02 Rotation bench

Local demonstration

SelectedOutside the rangeHeavier subtreeIn-order keys

Restore the balance.

Choose a node, then rotate its subtree. A balanced AVL tree has a balance factor of −1, 0 or 1 at every node: the height of the left subtree minus the height of the right.

Rotate right at 30 promotes 20. Node 30 has no right child, so it cannot rotate left.

On a node: arrow keys move between nodes, L or R rotates.

Node 30 has balance factor 2 (must be −1, 0 or 1). Its left child 20 also leans left (balance factor +1), so this is the LL case: rotate right at 30.

07 — Evaluation, results and limitations

The checks below describe the pinned repository. The accepted manuscript’s projected learning outcomes are outside the scope of this implementation review.

Repository facts with scope · Niraj-Chavan/nuerosymbolic-agentic-ai @ 87d8dd0
CheckFindingScopeEvidence
Test suite122 functionsMost cover AVL; none for red-black or segment tree.Counted; never run in CI
Violation injection5 testsAll on AVL trees.Counted in the repository
Continuous integration0 runsThe workflow file sits in a subfolder that GitHub does not read.Repository and Actions history

Limitations

  • The validators only see trees built by the tool’s own self-balancing code, so the symbolic path rarely fires in normal use.
  • A key mismatch between the diagnosis and teaching agents sends generic fallback text.
  • No persistence: state is held in memory across four workers.
  • Tests are thin outside AVL.
  • The documentation drifts from the code: it mentions a Claude adapter and React Flow, neither of which exists.
